name: SpatialSearch
title: Spatial Search
description: Search the platform knowledge base for the needs, skills, services and content most relevant to a query
whenToUse: Give an agent semantic search over the platform's own knowledge base: find the needs, skills, services and content most relevant to a query, and discover what else sits near a topic. Two searches in one, precise intent lookup and spatial discovery. Reach elsewhere when the knowledge lives in an external vector store. Attach by a service edge to the agent; it is not a data-flow step.

package.name: spatial
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

name: spatial
displayName: Spatial
version: 2.0.0
description: Semantic and spatial search over the platform's own knowledge base

# CALLS THE PLATFORM, NOT A VENDOR, which is what made this the last of the integration
# packages to migrate and what made two of its problems look bigger than they were.
#
# 1. AUTH. The retired node forwarded the caller's JWT as a bearer token, and §9.13 forbids a
#    manifest from holding one. That looked like a hard block. It was not: the runtime
#    listener is never published or proxied (AUTH_REMEDIATION.md, superseded July 2026 —
#    Docker network isolation IS the trust boundary), so a node calling the platform is
#    already inside it and needs no token. The retired client agreed without anyone noticing:
#    its `authHeaders` returned {} when there was none.
#
# 2. THE HOST. It read WORKFLOW_SERVICE_URL, a variable set NOWHERE in this repo, behind
#    `|| "http://localhost:4101"` — so the fallback was the entire behaviour, and a
#    deployment that moved the port would have failed at DNS naming a host nobody configured.
#    `scope.platformUrl` is derived from the port the runtime is actually listening on.
#
# What was genuinely missing was the CONTENT CARD lane, and that is now `renderCards` on a
# service method.

category: search

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, and deliberately just the numeric form: the allowedHosts pattern rejects a
  # bare "localhost", and `scope.platformUrl` is built from 127.0.0.1 anyway.
  #
  # This package must never reach a third-party host. Everything it knows is the platform's
  # own knowledge base, so a wildcard here would turn an internal search node into a way to
  # send that knowledge base somewhere else.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  transport: [json]
  # The card lane: a result row carrying a component renders it on the caller's live screen
  # the moment it surfaces. Declared because the executor implements it; a package naming it
  # on an older runtime would silently render nothing.
  renderCards: true

shared.entry.yaml:
# ONE ROW'S FULL AUTHORED CONTENT, projected for a model. Transcribed from readResult in the
# retired searchClient.
#
# The shaping is `helpers.entryRow` in shared/helpers.yaml, alongside the search projection it
# shares three functions with. This file is now only the part that is genuinely about
# readResult: what to say when the id does not exist.
#
# A MISS RETURNS A MESSAGE rather than throwing. The model has usually mistyped or invented an
# id, and "copy one verbatim from the conversation" is a recoverable instruction where an
# exception would end the turn.
project: >-
  return !response || !response.universal_id
    ? { error: 'No result with universal_id "' + String(params.universal_id)
        + '" — copy an id verbatim from a search result in this conversation.' }
    : helpers.entryRow(response)
shared.helpers.yaml:
# HOW ONE ROW IS SHAPED FOR A MODEL, as named functions rather than one long expression.
#
# The platform returns FULL rows: embeddings, UMAP coordinates, crawler metadata, raw image
# urls. A model needs a HANDLE plus the editorial essentials; the rest is context it wades
# through on every reasoning turn. With ref-hydration it must never see a raw image url at
# all, since it references a row by universal_id and the server fills in the bytes.
#
# These were one 45-line JavaScript blob inside a YAML scalar, and a second near-copy of the
# same logic in entry.yaml. Both searches and the depth read now call the same three
# functions, so "which fields does a promoted row keep" has ONE answer in ONE place.
#
# A helper sees only its arguments and its siblings: no config, no credentials, no caller
# scope. Same sandbox as every other expression, no extra authority.

helpers:
  # The editorial fields a row keeps, from whichever keep-list the caller passes.
  #
  # `reduce`, NOT `Object.assign({}, ...arr)`. Spread in CALL ARGUMENTS is banned by the
  # expression sandbox, and it used to fail at RUN time rather than at lint, so the node
  # reached the vendor, embedded the query, and died on the way back with
  # `disallowed expression: SpreadElement`.
  keptMeta:
    args: [metadata, keep]
    body: >-
      return keep
        .filter(k => (metadata || {})[k] != null && (metadata || {})[k] !== '')
        .reduce((acc, k) => Object.assign(acc, { [k]: metadata[k] }), {})

  # Whether a row has a picture, WITHOUT handing the model a url. `hasImage` is the flag it
  # reasons about; ref-hydration turns universal_id into bytes on the way out.
  hasImage:
    args: [row]
    body: >-
      return Boolean(
        (typeof (row.metadata || {}).primaryImage === 'string' && (row.metadata || {}).primaryImage)
          || (Array.isArray((row.metadata || {}).images) && (row.metadata || {}).images.length)
          || row.object_type === 'image'
      )

  # ONE SEARCH RESULT, projected. Used by findIntent and discoverRelated alike.
  #
  # NO bodyCopy: the full authored copy stays server-side and is fetched on demand by
  # readResult(universal_id). Lean by default, depth only when an answer needs it — the same
  # outline/readSection split SmartDocument uses.
  searchRow:
    args: [r]
    body: >-
      return ['skill', 'mcp', 'component'].includes(String(r.object_type))
        ? r
        : Object.assign(
            {
              universal_id: r.universal_id,
              object_type: r.object_type,
              title: r.title,
              description: r.description,
              key_need: r.key_need,
              source_url: r.source_url,
              hasImage: helpers.hasImage(r)
            },
            typeof r.similarity === 'number' ? { similarity: Math.round(r.similarity * 1000) / 1000 } : {},
            typeof r.distance === 'number' ? { distance: Math.round(r.distance * 10) / 10 } : {},
            typeof r.forQuery === 'string' ? { forQuery: r.forQuery } : {},
            // TWO SHAPES, TWO LISTS. A promoted service is authored copy and a card; a need is
            // extracted from a page and has none of those fields. Applying the service list to
            // a need kept nothing, not because a need has nothing worth keeping but because
            // none of its keys were on the list being asked for.
            ((meta) => Object.keys(meta).length ? { metadata: meta } : {})(
              helpers.keptMeta(
                r.metadata,
                (r.object_type === 'service' || (r.metadata || {}).promoted === true)
                  ? helpers.SEARCH_KEEP()
                  : helpers.NEED_KEEP()
              )
            )
          )

  # THE KEEP-LISTS, as functions because a helper takes arguments and returns a value — there
  # is no constant form. Based on the retired node's PROMOTED_META_KEEP, which the depth read
  # extended by three fields. Naming them here is what makes the difference between a search
  # row and a full read one readable line rather than two lists to diff by eye.
  #
  # `app` IS THE COMPONENT the row renders as, and it is the one addition to the retired list.
  #
  # The row already carries it, the card lane already draws it, and the agent harness's own
  # keep-list (agent-mcp/lean.ts MODEL_METADATA_FIELDS) explicitly includes it — but the
  # harness runs AFTER this projection and can only keep what this leaves, so stripping it
  # here made that intent unreachable. The model was describing courses whose cards were on
  # the screen in front of the person, with no way to know they were there.
  #
  # The retired node did not send it. That is a deliberate DIFFERENCE, not a transcription
  # slip: it costs about fifteen tokens a row and it is the only way the model can say "as
  # shown below" rather than restating a card the person is already looking at.
  SEARCH_KEEP:
    args: []
    body: >-
      return ['tagline', 'shortDescription', 'introParagraph', 'callToAction', 'actionPrompt',
              'app']

  # A NEED keeps ONE field: `action`, the short verb the page's own copy leads with
  # ("Advance Career", "Explore Jobs", "Check Requirements"). Title, description and key_need
  # already carry the substance; this is the only thing they say that those three do not.
  #
  # `questions` is deliberately OUT. Four full sentences a row, so ten needs is forty
  # sentences of suggested follow-ups the model did not ask for — the same context cost that
  # the whole lean projection exists to avoid.
  #
  # A NEW FIELD NEEDS BOTH HALVES. `action` had to be added to the agent harness's own
  # keep-list too (agent-mcp/lean.ts), because that projection runs AFTER this one and drops
  # anything it does not name. Adding it here alone would have changed nothing at all.
  NEED_KEEP:
    args: []
    body: "return ['action']"

  ENTRY_KEEP:
    args: []
    body: >-
      return ['tagline', 'shortDescription', 'introParagraph', 'callToAction', 'actionPrompt',
              'bodyCopy', 'mainCategory', 'section']

  # ONE ROW'S FULL AUTHORED CONTENT, for readResult. The complement of searchRow: same shape,
  # a wider keep-list, plus the row's own needs. Crawler bookkeeping (jsonLd, openGraph,
  # timestamps, paths) never reaches a model on either path.
  entryRow:
    args: [r]
    body: >-
      return Object.assign(
        {
          universal_id: r.universal_id,
          object_type: r.object_type,
          title: r.title,
          description: r.description,
          key_need: r.key_need,
          source_url: r.source_url,
          hasImage: helpers.hasImage(r)
        },
        (Array.isArray(r.needs) && r.needs.length) ? { needs: r.needs } : {},
        ((meta) => Object.keys(meta).length ? { metadata: meta } : {})(
          helpers.keptMeta(r.metadata, helpers.ENTRY_KEEP())
        )
      )
shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA.
#
# Transcribed VERBATIM from the retired SPATIAL_SCHEMA. This is the KNOWLEDGE PROTOCOL an
# attached agent follows and the argument shapes it fills in, so the wording IS the routing:
# rephrasing any of it changes how agents behave, and is never a tidy-up.
#
# Written as plain YAML rather than a `return { ... }` expression. A constant is data, and
# encoding a document this size inside a JavaScript string meant escaping every inner quote
# with no editor able to check the result.

spatial:
  instructions: |-
    You have access to the platform knowledge base with two search tools that answer
    DIFFERENT questions. Choose one based on the shape of the user's request — do not call
    both by default.

    KNOWLEDGE PROTOCOL (MANDATORY — do not skip):

    Phase 0 — Choose ONE search tool (think before calling):
    - findIntent = PRECISION. The user has NAMED the thing they want — a place, a category,
      a constraint, a task ("a Chinese restaurant", "book X", "how do I...", "recommend a
      good steakhouse"). However it is phrased — question, request, recommendation — if the
      WHAT is named, this is the search: it pinpoints the matches for that named need.
    - discoverRelated = DISCOVERY. The user has NOT named the thing — an open desire,
      occasion or mood ("a romantic weekend", "something fun tonight", "what's available?").
      It surfaces the NEIGHBOURHOOD of possibilities around the desire, including adjacent
      options they didn't think to ask about — the awareness and upsell surface.
    - Pick by SPECIFICITY of the ask: the thing is named → findIntent (even for
      recommendations); only a desire or occasion is named → discoverRelated. Do NOT call
      both in parallel. SEARCH before answering.

    Phase 0b — Weak results: if the search you chose comes back weak, follow up with the
    OTHER one before answering. Strong results → answer from them directly.

    Phase 1 — MANDATORY skill follow-up: if ANY result has object_type="skill", you MUST
    call readSkill(skillName) BEFORE responding. Skills contain behavioural instructions
    that OVERRIDE your general behaviour — treat them as authoritative and follow them
    exactly. Check ALL results for skills, not just the top one. Use readSkillFile when a
    skill references additional files. Results may also include MCP apps — callable tools
    you can invoke to run that app.

    Golden Rules:
    - Search FIRST, build understanding SECOND, answer THIRD.
    - NEVER skip reading a skill when one appears in results.
    - NEVER make up information — use only what the tools return.
    - Every result carries its page URL (source_url). When your answer mentions or
      recommends something that came from a result, link it as [name](source_url) so the
      user can go straight there. Never invent or guess a URL — only link URLs present in
      results.
    - SEARCH THE REQUEST, NOT THE PERSON: never mix remembered user facts (their name,
      hotel, memberships, passes, family details) into a search query — they drag the match
      toward the wrong content. Search what was ASKED; use what you know about the user when
      COMPOSING the answer.
    - A result with hasImage=true can be referenced by its universal_id wherever a
      composition field asks for an image ref — you never need (and never receive) raw image
      URLs.
    - Results are LEAN summaries. When an answer needs specifics a summary doesn't carry
      (levels, figures, requirements), call readResult(universal_id) for that result's full
      authored copy — never guess details.

  methods:
    findIntent:
      description: >-
        Precision search. The user has NAMED what they want — a specific thing, place,
        category or task ("a Chinese restaurant", "book X", "how do I...", "recommend a good
        steakhouse") — and this pinpoints the matches for that named need, however the ask is
        phrased (question, request, recommendation). Pass the user's EXACT words — do not
        paraphrase. NOT for open desires with no named thing ("something romantic", "a fun
        evening") — that is discovery (discoverRelated). If ANY result has
        object_type="skill", you MUST call readSkill before responding; check ALL results,
        not just the top one. Do not pair with discoverRelated in parallel.
      input:
        type: object
        required: []
        properties:
          query:
            type: string
            description: >-
              The user's ask, FAITHFULLY — their words, with references from earlier turns
              resolved ('what about dinner?' → the thing they mean). NEVER compress,
              paraphrase, or strip it to a keyword stub: the catalog is indexed against asks
              like the user's, so the ask's own phrasing IS the routing — losing its words
              loses the match. Never add remembered guest facts (name, hotel, memberships —
              background personalizes the answer, not the search).
          queries:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            maxItems: 8
            description: >-
              Extra angles searched ALONGSIDE the ask, never instead of it — the FIRST entry
              is always the user's faithful ask; add facets after it, one per entry. One
              round trip, all the material; each result carries forQuery.

    discoverRelated:
      description: >-
        Discovery search. For open desires where the user has NOT named the thing — an
        occasion, a mood, a vague wish ("a romantic weekend", "something fun with the kids",
        "what's available?"). Surfaces the NEIGHBOURHOOD of possibilities around the desire
        (content is grouped by need; nearby items are the adjacent choices), including
        options the user didn't think to ask about — the awareness and upsell surface. NOT
        for a named thing or category ("a Chinese restaurant" is findIntent). Also the
        follow-up when findIntent's results came back weak. Low similarity is normal — these
        are neighbours, not exact matches.
      input:
        type: object
        required: []
        properties:
          query:
            type: string
            description: >-
              The user's ask, FAITHFULLY — their words, with references from earlier turns
              resolved. NEVER compress, paraphrase, or strip it to a keyword stub: the
              catalog is indexed against asks like the user's, so the ask's own phrasing IS
              the routing — losing its words loses the match. Never add remembered guest
              facts (name, hotel, memberships — they drag the placement to the wrong region).
          queries:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            maxItems: 8
            description: >-
              Extra facets explored ALONGSIDE the ask, never instead of it — the FIRST entry
              is always the user's faithful ask; add facets after it, one per entry. Each
              result carries forQuery.

    readResult:
      description: >-
        Read the FULL content of one search result — its complete authored copy (bodyCopy),
        every detail the lean search row summarizes. Use when answering needs specifics the
        summary doesn't carry (levels, figures, requirements, routes). Pass the result's
        universal_id verbatim.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [universal_id]
        properties:
          universal_id:
            type: string
            description: The universal_id of a search result from this conversation, verbatim.

    readSkill:
      description: >-
        Read a skill's full instructions. MANDATORY whenever a search result has
        object_type="skill": skills contain behavioural instructions that OVERRIDE your
        general behaviour, and must be treated as authoritative and followed exactly.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [skillName]
        properties:
          skillName:
            type: string
            description: The skill's name, exactly as it appeared in the search result.

    readSkillFile:
      description: >-
        Read a file a skill references. Use when a skill's instructions point at another
        document; pass the path exactly as the skill wrote it.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [skillName, filePath]
        properties:
          skillName:
            type: string
            description: The skill that references the file.
          filePath:
            type: string
            description: The path as written in the skill's instructions.
shared.search.yaml:
# Everything the two searches share. They differ by ONE value, `mode`, so the body is written
# as an object of keys rather than as a single expression: a $ref with siblings merges and
# local wins, so a method overrides `mode` alone instead of restating thirty lines. Written
# as one expression it could only be replaced wholesale, and the two would drift.

# THE PLATFORM'S OWN SEARCH, on the loopback runtime. No credential and no forwarded token:
# the listener is never published or proxied, so a node calling it is already inside the
# trust boundary (AUTH_REMEDIATION.md, superseded July 2026).
#
# `scope.engineUrl` is the ENGINE on :4101, NOT `scope.platformUrl` (the runtime on :4106).
# Two internal listeners with different routes: search and dictionary reads are the engine's,
# while /skills below is the runtime's. Choosing wrongly is a bare 404 that reads like a
# missing route rather than the wrong service. The retired client had the same split hidden in
# two env vars, WORKFLOW_SERVICE_URL and UNOVERSE_SERVICE_URL, neither set anywhere in this
# repo — so both fallbacks were the entire behaviour.
call:
  name: search
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/spatial/search'"
  transport: json
  body:
    # OVERRIDDEN per method. Present here so the shape is complete and a method that forgets
    # to set it fails loudly at the server rather than silently searching one way.
    mode: "return params.__unset"

    # maxResults, the threshold and the type filters come from the NODE CONFIG, never from
    # the agent's arguments. That is this node's whole contract: the author decides what a
    # search may return, the model only decides what to ask for. A model that could widen its
    # own result set would route around the author.
    # `?? 10`, not `|| 10`, matching the retired node exactly. They differ on 0, which the
    # config's minimum of 5 makes unreachable today — but a fallback that fires on a
    # legitimate value is the same class of silent narrowing as the flags below, and there
    # is no reason to leave a second one in place.
    maxResults: "return config.maxResults != null ? Number(config.maxResults) : 10"
    workflowId: "return scope.workflowId"

    # PASSED THROUGH, NEVER COERCED. Each is `config.x` and nothing more, which is exactly
    # what the retired node did (`includeMcps: config?.includeMcps`).
    #
    # An UNSET flag must arrive as undefined so `resolveBody` drops the key and the SERVER's
    # own default applies — and those defaults are mostly TRUE (images, needs, services,
    # skills and mcps; only actions is false). Writing `=== true` turned every unset flag
    # into an explicit `false`, so a node whose author had not touched the toggles asked for
    # nothing instead of everything. Valid request, far narrower answer, no error.
    #
    # `false` is still SENT: resolveBody drops undefined and "", not false, so a deliberately
    # disabled type stays disabled.
    includeImages: "return config.includeImages"
    includeNeeds: "return config.includeNeeds"
    includeServices: "return config.includeServices"
    includeActions: "return config.includeActions"
    includeSkills: "return config.includeSkills"
    includeMcps: "return config.includeMcps"

    # A single ask, several angles, or both. `queries` batches ONE embedding call and N
    # searches into a single round trip, each row tagged with the query it answered.
    #
    # Both resolve to undefined when unset, and `resolveBody` DROPS a key that resolves to
    # nothing — which is what is wanted here: the server distinguishes an absent `queries`
    # from an empty one.
    query: "return String(params.query || '').trim() || undefined"
    queries: "return (Array.isArray(params.queries) && params.queries.length) ? params.queries : undefined"

    # OMITTED when unset so the SERVER's default floor applies. Sending 0 would mean "keep
    # everything", which is a different instruction from "use the platform default" and was a
    # real behavioural difference in the retired client.
    similarityThreshold: >-
      return (config.similarityThreshold != null && String(config.similarityThreshold) !== '')
        ? Number(config.similarityThreshold) : undefined

  error:
    when: "return !response || !Array.isArray(response.results)"
    message: "return 'spatial/search failed: ' + JSON.stringify(response || {}).slice(0, 300)"

# THE MODEL-FACING REPLY.
#
# THE NODE PROJECTS. Legacy did — `{ ...result, results: projectResultsForModel(result.results) }`
# — and the agent harness ALSO leans the reply afterwards. Two projections, and that is not an
# accident to be tidied away: the harness's is a generic floor for any search-shaped tool, and
# this one is spatial's own contract, which knows `bodyCopy` belongs behind readResult and that
# a plain need keeps no metadata at all.
#
# Removing this on 2026-07-29, on the theory that the harness could own it alone, put the FULL
# rows into the reply: jsonLd, openGraph, UMAP coordinates, every bodyCopy in full. Roughly
# 100k tokens per search, and every one of them recorded into node_traces as well. The harness
# lean is not a replacement for this; it runs after it.
#
# THE WHOLE ENVELOPE, not a bare array. `queryPoint` and `count` survive, and the harness reads
# `parsed.results` — a bare array makes its own projection no-op silently.
#
# The row shaping is `helpers.searchRow` in shared/helpers.yaml, where it can be read and
# diffed as a named function rather than 45 lines inside this scalar.
#
# Evaluated AFTER the card lane, which needs the full rows.
lean: >-
  return Object.assign({}, response, { results: (response.results || []).map(helpers.searchRow) })

files.api/service.yaml:
# THE FIVE TOOLS an attached agent gets. Descriptions transcribed VERBATIM from the retired
# SPATIAL_SCHEMA: they are what the model reads when choosing a tool, so their wording is the
# routing. Rephrasing them is a behaviour change, not a tidy-up.

findIntent:
  description: >-
    Precision search. The user has NAMED what they want, a specific thing, place, category or
    task ("a Chinese restaurant", "book X", "how do I...", "recommend a good steakhouse"),
    and this pinpoints the matches for that named need, however the ask is phrased. Pass the
    user's EXACT words, do not paraphrase. NOT for open desires with no named thing
    ("something romantic", "a fun evening"), which is discoverRelated. If ANY result has
    object_type="skill" you MUST call readSkill before responding; check ALL results, not
    just the top one. Do not pair with discoverRelated in parallel.
  calls:
    - $ref: search#call
      body:
        mode: "return 'intent'"
  # THE CARD LANE. A result row carrying a component renders it on the caller's live screen
  # the moment it surfaces: data-driven, never a model tool, so the model cannot forget to
  # show it or describe one that is not there. Declared BEFORE `returns` because a card needs
  # the full row that the lean projection strips.
  #
  # Unconditional on purpose. This was a config toggle until 2026-07-29 and it was the wrong
  # shape: a row only produces a card when it points at one, so "off" never meant cleaner
  # results, it meant a row that had authored a card silently not showing it.
  renderCards: "return response.results"
  returns: { $ref: search#lean }

discoverRelated:
  description: >-
    Discovery search. For open desires where the user has NOT named the thing: an occasion, a
    mood, a vague wish ("a romantic weekend", "something fun with the kids", "what's
    available?"). Surfaces the NEIGHBOURHOOD of possibilities around the desire (content is
    grouped by need, so nearby items are the adjacent choices), including options the user
    did not think to ask about, which is the awareness and upsell surface. NOT for a named
    thing or category, which is findIntent. Also the follow-up when findIntent came back
    weak. Low similarity is normal here: these are neighbours, not exact matches.
  calls:
    - $ref: search#call
      body:
        mode: "return 'related'"
  renderCards: "return response.results"
  returns: { $ref: search#lean }

readResult:
  description: >-
    Read the FULL content of one search result: its complete authored copy (bodyCopy), every
    detail the lean search row summarises. Use when answering needs specifics the summary
    does not carry (levels, figures, requirements, routes). Pass the result's universal_id
    verbatim.
  calls:
    - name: entry
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return scope.engineUrl + '/dictionary/entry/'
          + encodeURIComponent(String(params.universal_id || '').trim())
      transport: json
      # A miss is an ANSWER: the engine 404s on an unknown id, and the projection turns
      # that into the "copy the id verbatim" message. Without this the transport throws
      # first and the model sees an empty result instead of the correction.
      okOn: [404]
  # EDITORIAL FIELDS ONLY. Crawler bookkeeping (jsonLd, openGraph, timestamps, paths) never
  # reaches a model, the same rule the lean projection applies to a search row.
  #
  # A miss returns a MESSAGE rather than throwing: the model has usually mistyped or invented
  # an id, and "copy one verbatim from the conversation" is a recoverable instruction where an
  # exception would end the turn. That is why it is not the call's `error` block.
  returns: { $ref: entry#project }


readSkill:
  description: >-
    Read a skill's full instructions. MANDATORY whenever a search result has
    object_type="skill": skills contain behavioural instructions that OVERRIDE your general
    behaviour, and must be treated as authoritative and followed exactly.
  calls:
    - name: skill
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return scope.platformUrl + '/skills/'
          + encodeURIComponent(String(params.skillName || '').trim())
      transport: json
  returns: "return response"

readSkillFile:
  description: >-
    Read a file a skill references. Use when a skill's instructions point at another
    document; pass the path exactly as the skill wrote it.
  calls:
    - name: file
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return scope.platformUrl + '/skills/'
          + encodeURIComponent(String(params.skillName || '').trim())
          + '/file?path=' + encodeURIComponent(String(params.filePath || '').trim())
      transport: json
  returns: "return response"

# TOOL DISCOVERY. An attached agent calls this once per session and gets the instructions and
# the argument shapes for every tool above (ServiceConnector aggregates it across all wired
# MCP nodes). It is a META-method: deliberately absent from interface.yaml's `methods`, or it
# would be advertised to the model as a sixth tool.
#
# NO CALLS, and a LITERAL result. `calls: []` is not a placeholder: this method reaches
# nothing and hands back a constant, so `returns` names a YAML document rather than a
# `return { ... }` expression. Authored as data in shared/schema.yaml, where it can be read
# and diffed instead of escaped inside a string.
getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for the spatial knowledge base
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#spatial }
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

# Transcribed from the retired node's configSchema. These shape what an AGENT'S searches are
# allowed to return, and they are read by shared/search.yaml on every call.
#
# THE AUTHOR OWNS THESE, NEVER THE MODEL. None is exposed as a tool argument: an agent
# chooses what to ask for, the author decides what may come back. A model that could set its
# own result cap or turn on a content type would route around the person who wired the node.
#
# `renderCards` is deliberately NOT here. It was a toggle until 2026-07-29 and was the wrong
# shape: a row only produces a card when it points at one, so "off" never meant cleaner
# results, it meant a row that had authored a card silently not showing it.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    maxResults:
      type: number
      title: Max Results
      description: Maximum total results to return (safety cap)
      default: 10
      minimum: 5
      maximum: 30

    similarityThreshold:
      type: number
      title: Min Similarity (Intent)
      description: >-
        Precision floor for findIntent (0 to 0.9). Results scoring below this cosine
        similarity are dropped. Discovery is unaffected, since it ranks by spatial distance.
      default: 0.35
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 0.9
      step: 0.05

    # The six type filters, matching the Spatial view panel's vocabulary. Each maps to one
    # flag on /spatial/search.
    includeNeeds:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Needs
      description: Fetch needs from results
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle

    includeImages:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Images
      description: Fetch images from results
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle

    includeServices:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Services
      description: Fetch services from results
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle

    includeActions:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Actions
      description: Fetch actions from results
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle

    includeSkills:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Skills
      # The one that defaults ON, matching the retired node. Skills carry behavioural
      # instructions an agent is REQUIRED to follow, so losing them silently changes how the
      # agent behaves rather than just what it finds.
      description: Fetch skills (behavioural instructions)
      default: true
      "ui:widget": toggle

    includeMcps:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Apps
      # "Apps", matching the view panel and the server, which folds object_type "mcp" and
      # "component" into ONE Apps family (routes/dictionary/search.ts). The old "Include MCP"
      # label named half of what the flag controls.
      description: Fetch apps and MCP workflows from results
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # It matters more here than on most nodes: this searches the platform's OWN knowledge
    # base, so a workflow that should only answer signed-in staff says so with this toggle
    # rather than by hoping the trigger was set correctly.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, maxResults, similarityThreshold, includeNeeds, includeImages, includeServices, includeActions, includeSkills, includeMcps]
files.interface.yaml:
# A PURE SERVICE NODE: no inputs, no outputs. The graph never runs it; an agent calls it over
# a service edge and gets one value back. That is why there is no api/events.yaml here, and
# why declaring an output would create a dot nothing could ever fire.

inputs: []
outputs: []

serviceConnectors:
  - name: knowledgeSearch
    serviceType: mcp
    # PROVIDES. The node offers these tools to a consuming agent rather than consuming
    # anything itself.
    isService: true
    description: Semantic and spatial search tools for an agent
    # `getSchema` is deliberately absent: it is tool DISCOVERY, a meta-method the harness
    # calls, not one of the tools on offer. Listing it would advertise it to the model.
    methods:
      - findIntent
      - discoverRelated
      - readResult
      - readSkill
      - readSkillFile
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

# Transcribed from _legacy/nodes/spatial/src/SpatialSearch. Every tool, every instruction
# string and the model-facing projection are carried over verbatim; see api/service.yaml.

type: SpatialSearch

# THE TYPE IS REUSED, unlike email and pinecone where it deliberately was not. Nothing about
# the contract changes here: same tools, same arguments, same platform endpoints, same
# results. The token that used to be forwarded was never read by anything (loopback), so a
# workflow wired to this node keeps behaving identically. There is nothing for an author to
# decide, so there is no decision to force on them.

kind: PromiseNode

# HOW THE CANVAS DRAWS IT. Every other service node in the tree says this — HubspotMCP,
# SalesforceMCP, SlackMCP, DynamoDBService, BedrockEmbeddingService — and the retired node
# said it too (`template: "service"` in its definition).
#
# Omitting it is not cosmetic: a service node has NO connectors, so the ordinary card draws
# input and output dots that can never carry anything, and invites someone to wire it into
# the data flow instead of attaching it to an agent. The service card shows the attachment
# point, which is the only way this node is ever reached.

template: service

name: Spatial Search
category: Search
color: "#8b5cf6"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  Search the platform knowledge base for the needs, skills, services and content most
  relevant to a query

whenToUse: >-
  Give an agent semantic search over the platform's own knowledge base: find the needs,
  skills, services and content most relevant to a query, and discover what else sits near a
  topic. Two searches in one, precise intent lookup and spatial discovery. Reach elsewhere
  when the knowledge lives in an external vector store. Attach by a service edge to the
  agent; it is not a data-flow step.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13).
#
# `required: false`, and that is a considered answer rather than the default one. This node
# reads the platform's OWN knowledge base, so demanding sign-in here would break every public
# experience built on it: a guest asking a concierge agent a question is exactly the case it
# exists for. What a guest may reach is decided at the door by the trigger's publicEntry
# toggle, which is where an audience decision belongs, and a workflow that should be
# staff-only says so with the instance toggle on this box.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable. The index changes as content is ingested, and a service method answering
  # from a stale cache would tell an agent something is not there when it is. Reuse is also
  # worth less than it looks: the queries are the user's own words and rarely repeat.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# A SERVICE node has no connectors, so the fixture names a METHOD and asserts the value it
# hands back. `findIntent` because it exercises the whole chain that matters: the loopback
# url from scope.platformUrl, the config-owned filters, and the lean projection.
#
# Runs against the LOCAL platform, so it needs the runtime up. No credential: the search API
# is reached on loopback, inside the trust boundary.

testData:
  config:
    maxResults: 5
    similarityThreshold: 0
    includeNeeds: true
    includeServices: true
    includeSkills: true
  call:
    method: findIntent
    params:
      query: What is there to do this weekend?
  expect:
    # THE PROJECTION IS THE ASSERTION. An empty result set is a legitimate answer (the index
    # is the tester's), so this checks the SHAPE every row must have rather than any content:
    # a handle, and none of the heavy fields the projection exists to strip.
    #
    # `embedding` and `umap` leaking through is the exact regression this guards — it is what
    # sent 100k tokens of vectors into a model's context before the lean pass existed.
    result: >-
      return Array.isArray(output)
        && output.every(r =>
          typeof r.universal_id === 'string'
            && r.embedding === undefined
            && r.umap === undefined
            && r.metadata?.bodyCopy === undefined)
